title: Strict Roos comparison and integral completeness across a finite clopen cover
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-pur-conventions].

Write $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $r_i$ for restriction of its module sheaves and complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A strict tower consists of complexes $C_n$ and chain maps $t_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$, with morphisms the compatible families of chain maps. Restriction and sectionwise product gluing are inverse equivalences on these strict towers. Restriction identifies termwise countable products with the component products, carries the endomorphism $(c_n)_n\mapsto(c_n-t_n(c_{n+1}))_n$ to the identical component formula, and induces a natural chain isomorphism
$$r_i\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_C)[-1]\cong\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_{r_iC})[-1].$$
This comparison is compatible with strict tower maps and their projections. On derived categories it preserves the derived-limit property, with its specified Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit]. In particular the actual reduction maps $K\to\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$ and the transitions restrict to the corresponding component maps [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-reduction-tower].

Derived completeness [def-weil-derived-complete] is equivalent to derived completeness of every component, retaining the specified first map to the product in the Roos triangle. Membership in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] is equivalent to componentwise membership. Membership in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] is likewise equivalent to componentwise membership. For both the cohomological supports of all positive reductions and their Tor amplitudes, any common bounds for the finite list of component bounds uniform in $n$ are uniform bounds on $X$.

The unbounded restriction equivalence therefore restricts to these two integral full subcategories. It preserves completed tensor products and their coefficient units as defined by the strict reduction towers in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. For every finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset L$, it commutes naturally with the integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], including the level maps to $A_{L,m}$ and their transitions. No canonical cone is asserted in a bare triangulated category: functoriality refers to the displayed strict complex model. All assertions include the empty partition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] with $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$. Its exact restriction/gluing equivalence identifies the coefficient rings, their quotient projections and all coefficient transitions. Apply the two functors degreewise and at each tower level; give the glued tower transition $G((t_{i,n})_i)$ and a glued tower morphism $G((f_{i,n})_i)$. The chain-map and transition-compatibility equations hold because they hold in every component and the module equivalence is faithful. Its natural unit and counit commute with these maps by naturality, so they give inverse equivalences on strict towers, including their morphisms.

proof.text: Countable products are sectionwise by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. For $U\to X_i$, its pullback to $X_j$ is empty for $j\ne i$, while its pullback to $X_i$ is $U$. Thus restriction identifies $(\prod_n C_n)^m(U)$ with $\prod_n(r_iC_n)^m(U)$, with the same projections and differential. Conversely the product reindexing $\prod_n\prod_i F_{i,n}(U\times_X X_i)\cong\prod_i\prod_n F_{i,n}(U\times_X X_i)$ identifies products under gluing. Each reindexing is the identity on its $(i,n)$ coordinate; hence it preserves restriction maps, module actions and every product projection.

source.place: Tags 08TC/07KC, definition-derived-limit and lemma-products; explicit finite-clopen application by the worker.

proof.text: Put $P_C=\prod_nC_n$ and $v_C=1-s_C$. The $n$th projection of $r_iv_C$ is $r_i\operatorname{pr}_n-r_it_n\,r_i\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$, so under step 2 it is exactly the $n$th projection of $v_{r_iC}$. Use the explicit model [def-weil-strict-roos-model]: in degree $m$ its shifted cone is $P_C^{m-1}\oplus P_C^m$ with $d(y,x)=(-dy-v_Cx,dx)$. Apply the product comparisons of step 2 separately to $y$ and $x$. Additivity of restriction and the displayed equality for $v$ make this a chain isomorphism with inverse the two inverse product comparisons. A strict tower map $f$ acts diagonally by $(\prod_nf_n,\prod_nf_n)$, so both orders of composing the comparisons have the same two coordinates. The cone projection to $P_C$ is $(y,x)\mapsto x$ and the connecting map $P_C\to\operatorname{Cone}(v_C)[-1][1]$ is $z\mapsto(-z,0)$ with this Roos-triangle convention. These formulas commute with restriction, retaining every level projection. This is strict-complex functoriality.

proof.text: The exact countable products supplied by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] meet the hypothesis of [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core], on $X$ and on each $X_i$. Therefore the termwise product cones of step 2 represent the actual products in the derived categories. The triangulated restriction equivalence of [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus] sends distinguished triangles to the component distinguished triangles. Applying it to the triangle in [def-weil-derived-limit], with the same product projections, sends $1-s$ to $1-s$ by step 3 and retains both triangle maps. Conversely a tuple of such distinguished Roos triangles is a distinguished triangle in the product triangulated category, and its inverse image is distinguished under the inverse equivalence. Thus the derived-limit property with its specified triangle is preserved in both directions.

source.place: Tags 08TC/07KC, definition-derived-limit and lemma-products; explicit finite-clopen application by the worker.

proof.text: Represent $K$ by $q:P\to K$ as in [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. The K-flatness and flat-term assertions in [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus] show that $r_iP\to r_iK$ is an admissible resolution. Its termwise change-of-rings comparison identifies $r_i(P\otimes_R(A_{E,n})_X)$ with $r_iP\otimes_{R_i}(A_{E,n})_{X_i}$. On tensors it sends $p\otimes a$ to $r_ip\otimes r_ia$. Consequently it sends $\gamma_n(p)=p\otimes1$ to the component $\gamma_n$, and $\tau_n(p\otimes a)=p\otimes\rho_n(a)$ to the component $\tau_n$, because the coefficient identifications preserve $1$ and $\rho_n$. Exact restriction also sends $[q]^{-1}$ to $[r_iq]^{-1}$. Hence the actual $c_n=[\gamma_n][q]^{-1}$, not merely their source and target objects, and the transitions $t_n=[\tau_n]$ are identified. This proves the required reduction comparison on objects and maps.

source.place: Tags 08TC/07KC, definition-derived-limit and lemma-products; explicit finite-clopen application by the worker.

proof.text: In [def-weil-derived-complete] the first triangle map is the fixed $c=(c_n)_n$. Step 5 and the product projections identify $r_ic$ with $(c_{i,n})_n$. If $K$ is complete, step 4 restricts its witnessing distinguished triangle to the required one on each component. Conversely choose the witnessing connecting map $\delta_i$ for each complete $r_iK$. The full and faithful derived equivalence of [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus] gives a unique morphism $\delta:\prod_nK_n\to K[1]$ corresponding to this tuple, using the product and shift identifications. The triangle with maps $c,1-s,\delta$ corresponds to the tuple of the witnessing distinguished triangles, so is distinguished by that equivalence. This proves completeness without changing $c$ or choosing a functorial cone in the bare triangulated category.

source.place: Tags 08TC/07KC, definition-derived-limit and lemma-products; explicit finite-clopen application by the worker.

proof.text: For every $n\ge1$, step 5 identifies the restriction of the $n$th reduction with the $n$th component reduction. Apply [lem-pur-clopen-finite-constructibility-bounds] to these finite coefficients: constructibility and cohomological vanishing in a fixed interval are detected componentwise, as is Tor amplitude in a fixed interval. By [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the integral constructible condition is exactly completeness, constructibility of all reductions, and one cohomological interval independent of $n$. If component $i$ has interval $[a_i,b_i]$ independent of $n$, choose $a=\min_i a_i$, $b=\max_i b_i$; this interval works on $X$ for every $n$. Any larger common interval also works. The same argument with the Tor intervals $[u_i,v_i]$ and [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] proves the integral $ctf$ assertion. Restricting global intervals gives the converse. The derived equivalence therefore restricts to both full subcategories: its inverse glues tuples that satisfy these conditions.

source.place: Tags 08TC/07KC, definition-derived-limit and lemma-products; explicit finite-clopen application by the worker.

proof.text: For the completed tensor of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], choose its K-flat flat-term resolutions $P,Q$. By [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus] their restrictions are such resolutions on every component, and its termwise tensor comparison identifies the reduction-level complex $P_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}Q_n$ with the tensor of the two component reductions. On pure tensors the transition is $(p\otimes a)\otimes(q\otimes b)\mapsto(p\otimes\rho_n a)\otimes(q\otimes\rho_n b)$; restriction gives exactly this formula on $X_i$. Thus this is an isomorphism of strict towers, including all transitions and maps. Apply the natural strict-cone comparison of step 3 to obtain the completed tensor comparison; the well-defined operation of the cited definition makes it independent of the resolutions. The coefficient unit restricts to the coefficient unit since $r_iR=R_i$ with its section $1$ by [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing]; its finite quotient units and all transitions are preserved as well. This proves preservation of the completed tensor and its coefficient units.

source.place: Tags 08TC/07KC, definition-derived-limit and lemma-products; explicit finite-clopen application by the worker.

proof.text: For $E\subset L$, use exactly the maps $\rho_m:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}\to(A_{L,m})_X$ and complexes $P_{L,m}=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}}(A_{L,m})_X$ in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. The coefficient identifications of [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] for $E$ and $L$ preserve quotient projections and the maps induced by the constant coefficient inclusion. The derived extension-of-scalars and termwise tensor comparisons of [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus] consequently identify $r_iP_{L,m}$ with $(r_iP)_{L,m}$. Their pure-tensor formula sends $p\otimes a$ to $r_ip\otimes r_ia$, so commutes with the map $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ at every level and with each transition $p\otimes a\mapsto p\otimes\bar a$. Restriction of scalars here merely reads the same complex via the corresponding coefficient projection, so these comparisons also identify the strict towers of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L}$-modules. Step 3 for the $L$-coefficient ring gives the scalar-extension comparison. Its diagonal formula on strict tower maps, together with the well-defined scalar-extension functor in the cited definition, gives naturality on derived morphisms.

source.place: Tags 08TC/07KC, definition-derived-limit and lemma-products; explicit finite-clopen application by the worker.

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, the covering hypothesis forces $X=\varnothing$. By [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] its module category is zero, as are its complex and derived categories. All towers, maps and Roos triangles are the zero ones. The zero object has every cohomological and Tor interval, so take $[0,0]$ when no component supplies bounds. Empty individual components contribute only zero factors and may be omitted. Thus all comparisons, completeness conditions, full-subcategory equivalences and uniform-bound assertions above include the empty partition.
